correctness.rationale: For every strictly realized spectral mask, the global Lipschitz norm reduces exactly to the projected-step path-variation norm. Its Haar-band upper bound is proved by an explicit block-amplitude inequality and one Haar coefficient per step per band. Its lower bound is the exact binomial expectation over all independent Bernoulli masks; the first-edge contribution is 1/2 and each other edge is a sum of n/2 Rademacher signs divided by n. The count, normalizations, edge boundaries, attainment and n=2 case have been checked algebraically, with exhaustive finite mask/step testing at n=2,4,8 and random strict-chamber checks at larger sizes.

value.rationale: The stability of coefficient shrinkage depends sharply on the transform and sample adjacency, despite Hilbert nonexpansivity. The theorem gives the correct unbounded dimension exponent on a natural ordered signal domain; its exact random spectral mask impulse mean has a direct probabilistic and robust-filtering interpretation, and distinguishes Walsh from Haar and Hamming-cube geometries.
